title: Show each dashboard panel as soon as it is ready

blocks.text: The on-call engineers open the operations dashboard first thing in an incident. It has a dozen panels, and each panel runs its own query on a pool. The complaint: the dashboard stays blank for forty seconds whenever the weekly-revenue panel's query is slow, even though the error rate and the queue depth, the two panels anyone looks at during an incident, were ready almost at once.
The screen can show a panel from any thread. Write the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Dashboard.java`:

items: `load(...)`: run the panels' queries and put each panel on the screen.

blocks.text: When you're done, each panel appears as soon as its own query has answered, a query that fails shows its panel as `unavailable` without keeping the others off the screen, and `load` returns once every panel is shown. About twelve lines in total.
The tests run the queries on a real `ExecutorService` and hold some of them with latches.

cases.says: every panel ends up on the screen with its query's answer
a panel whose query has answered is shown while a slower query is still running, whatever order the panels were given in
a failed query shows its panel as unavailable, and the other panels still appear

origin.section: Futures Read in Submission Order Wait for the Slowest; a CompletionService Hands Them Back as They Finish

concepts: Reading futures in submission order waits for the slowest first; a CompletionService hands each future back as its task completes.
